name: Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc.

profile.description: Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. is an energy infrastructure company providing distributed behind-the-meter power solutions for AI data centers, industrial loads, and oil and gas operations. Formerly Solaris Oilfield Infrastructure, the company renamed in September 2024 after acquiring Mobile Energy Rentals (MER), pivoting from frac sand logistics into natural gas-powered turbine leasing for hyperscaler data centers. Q2 2026 revenue of $219.4M grew 47% YoY with adjusted EBITDA of $108.3M. The company operates approximately 3,100 MW of total power generation capacity with over 2 GW under long-term contracts (10-15 year terms) with leading global technology companies. Completed nearly $2B in financing ($1.3B senior unsecured notes + $650M revolving credit facility).

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Solaris executed one of the most dramatic business transformations in the energy sector, pivoting from oilfield frac sand logistics to AI data center power infrastructure. Q2 2026 revenue of $219.4M grew 47% YoY, with Power Solutions segment revenue of $158.3M and ~950 MW average earning revenue [1]. The company expanded three long-term contracts expected to add over $100M of annual adjusted EBITDA, including a turnkey ~660 MW power plant for an AI workload customer [1]. The MER and Genco Power Solutions acquisitions expanded capacity to ~3,100 MW. AI Deployment (1/2): Solaris does not deploy AI in its operations but is a critical physical enabler of AI infrastructure. Natural gas turbines provide the power AI data centers require. Some operational analytics likely used but AI is not a product differentiator. Market Share (1/2): Solaris is an emerging leader in distributed behind-the-meter power for data centers, with 3,100 MW total capacity and 2+ GW contracted with hyperscalers [2]. The market is early-stage with many new entrants scaling. Product Pipeline (2/2): Exceptional forward visibility. Contracted capacity phases in through 2029 with 10-15 year terms. The expanded contracts adding $100M+ annual EBITDA and 660 MW turnkey power plant provide near-term growth visibility. Target of 3.1 GW net owned by 2029 with projected $1.7B revenue [2][3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Significant capital investment in new turbine technology (NovaLT16 diversifies equipment base) and $2B in financing to fund capacity expansion [1].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Founder Bill Zartler built Solaris from startup through IPO and now a dramatic transformation. The emerging mission of 'powering the digital economy' through behind-the-meter data center infrastructure has genuine purpose, but the company articulates this primarily in financial terms. The September 2024 rebrand from Solaris Oilfield Infrastructure signals the pivot, but continued frac sand logistics operations ($61.1M Q2 revenue) suggest the pivot is more opportunistic than mission-driven [1][3]. Community Impact (1/2): The Inspire Impact Score of 20 (MIXED) with positive attributions for Business Ethics, Business Resilience, and GHG Emissions reflects some ESG commitment [4]. Natural gas turbines are cleaner than diesel alternatives in temporary power. However, fossil fuel-based power generation inherently limits environmental inspiration. Employee Retention (1/2): The 468-person team has executed a remarkable transformation — pivoting from oilfield services to data center power, completing multiple acquisitions, and integrating new capabilities. The co-CEO structure (Zartler and Johnson) provides leadership continuity. Limited public data on culture metrics. Insider Buying (0/2): Significant insider selling of $2.8M over the past 3 months undermines conviction signals. The 87.6% increase in shares outstanding over one year from financing and equity issuances creates substantial dilution for existing shareholders [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics as a Growth stock. Q2 2026 delivered strong results: revenue $219.4M (+47% YoY), net income $25.2M ($0.26/diluted share), adjusted EBITDA $108.3M (+30% sequential) [1]. Profit margin improved to 11.5% (up from 6.69% in Q1), reflecting operating leverage as Power Solutions scales [1]. PEG of ~0.9 scores 1.0 with 2x growth weight — the growth rate exceeds the earnings multiple. D/E of ~146% scores 0.67 (elevated due to $2B financing package including $1.3B notes and $650M revolver) [1]. ROE of ~8% scores 0.53 with 2x growth weight. Forward P/E of ~32 scores 0.70. Revenue growth of 47% YoY scores 1.0. The 87.6% year-over-year increase in shares outstanding represents significant equity dilution from financing activities [5]. Company raised Q3/Q4 guidance following strong Q2 results. Liquidity floor cleared: avg daily volume ~2.35M at ~$80 = ~$188M daily turnover.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Solaris is one of the most directly AI-benefiting business models in the energy sector. The company provides physical power generation equipment that AI data centers require — every GPU running AI workloads needs electricity, and Solaris supplies it through natural gas turbines leased on 10-15 year terms to investment-grade technology companies [1][2]. AI cannot substitute for physical power generation; it can only increase demand. The Q2 expansion of three contracts adding $100M+ annual EBITDA and the 660 MW turnkey power plant for an AI customer underscore accelerating demand [1]. The distributed behind-the-meter model addresses a critical bottleneck — grid capacity constraints force hyperscalers to procure on-site power [2][3]. The only risk is potential technology shifts (nuclear SMRs, grid modernization) that could reduce gas turbine demand over the 10-15 year horizon, but near-term AI power demand far exceeds alternatives. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI is Solaris's primary growth catalyst. Revenue from technology company contracts is surging, with Power Solutions generating $158.3M in Q2 (72% of total revenue) with segment EBITDA of $96.4M [1]. The pivot from oilfield services was entirely driven by AI power demand, and the $1.7B 2029 revenue target is fundamentally an AI data center power thesis [3].

infinite_game.summary: Solaris under Bill Zartler demonstrates exceptional existential flexibility — the pivot from oilfield services to AI data center power is a textbook Sinek transformation. However, the Just Cause remains underdeveloped (more opportunistic than mission-driven), significant insider selling and share dilution raise concerns about leadership alignment, and limited visibility into organizational culture prevents full assessment. The company makes bold long-term bets (10-15 year contracts, $2B financing) while still operating in the inherently cyclical energy services sector.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Solaris's emerging cause of 'powering the digital economy' through reliable energy infrastructure has genuine purpose, but the company articulates this primarily in financial terms — yields, EBITDA, and contract values [1][2]. The continued operation of frac sand logistics ($61.1M Q2 revenue) alongside power solutions suggests the pivot is opportunistic rather than cause-driven [1]. Zartler's 30+ years in energy investing suggests a financially-driven leadership style. The strategic brilliance of the pivot is undeniable, but it followed demand signals rather than a pre-existing Just Cause.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The 468-person team successfully executed a dramatic business transformation — pivoting operations, completing multiple acquisitions (MER, Genco), integrating new capabilities, and closing $2B in financing — which implies strong internal alignment [1][3]. The co-CEO structure provides collaborative leadership. However, the rapid growth (87.6% share dilution, massive capacity expansion) could stress organizational cohesion, and limited public data on culture prevents thorough assessment.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Solaris competes in distributed power with established players and new entrants attracted by AI demand. The company differentiates through scale (3,100 MW), long-term contracted revenue (2+ GW under 10-15 year terms), and equipment diversity (NovaLT16 diversification) [1][2]. The willingness to partner with hyperscalers on turnkey solutions (660 MW power plant) rather than merely lease equipment shows adaptive competitive positioning.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): The transformation from Solaris Oilfield Infrastructure to Solaris Energy Infrastructure is a textbook existential pivot — leveraging existing equipment logistics capabilities for an entirely new purpose (powering AI data centers instead of frac operations) [1][2][3]. The acquisitions (MER, Genco), name change, and 10-15 year contract structure demonstrate willingness to fundamentally reshape the business. Q2 2026 shows the Power Solutions segment now generates 72% of total revenue ($158.3M of $219.4M), confirming the transformation's success [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Zartler made a genuinely courageous bet pivoting to data center power. The $2B financing package ($1.3B notes + $650M revolver) and the 660 MW turnkey power plant commitment represent deep conviction [1]. However, significant insider selling ($2.8M in 3 months) and the 87.6% share dilution over one year create tension — the company is growing aggressively but at substantial cost to existing shareholders' ownership [5]. Bold infrastructure bets are partially offset by financial engineering that dilutes the founders' and shareholders' stakes.

investment_thesis: Solaris Energy Infrastructure is one of the purest plays on the AI power infrastructure bottleneck, with over 2 GW of natural gas power generation contracted under 10-15 year terms with investment-grade technology companies [1][2]. Q2 2026 delivered $219.4M revenue (+47% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of $108.3M (+30% sequential), and Power Solutions now represents 72% of revenue [1]. The expansion of three contracts adding $100M+ annual EBITDA and a turnkey 660 MW power plant for an AI customer demonstrate accelerating demand [1]. PEG of ~0.9 — below 1.0 — is exceptional for a company growing revenue at 47%. Profit margin improved to 11.5% (from 6.69%) as operating leverage materializes. The $2B financing package provides capital to execute the capacity expansion toward 3.1 GW and $1.7B revenue by 2029 [2][3]. Grid capacity constraints structurally favor distributed behind-the-meter power, and Solaris is the scaled leader.
thesis_continued: The primary risks are financial leverage and dilution. D/E of ~146% and $2B in new financing create substantial debt burden, with operating cash flow covering only 20% of total debt [5]. The 87.6% increase in shares outstanding over one year represents dramatic dilution — existing shareholders' ownership has been nearly halved to fund the capacity expansion, and further equity issuances may be needed [5]. Insider selling of $2.8M over 3 months is concerning for a founder-led company, suggesting even management is reducing exposure despite bullish operational momentum. Profit margin of 11.5% is improving but still thin for an infrastructure company, and GAAP EPS of $0.26/quarter underperforms the adjusted $0.39 due to non-cash charges. Trailing PE of 77x prices in significant future earnings that must materialize from contracted capacity converting to revenue. Technology risk from nuclear SMRs and grid buildouts could reduce long-term demand for gas distributed power, and the legacy frac sand business ($61.1M Q2) remains exposed to oilfield cyclicality.
key_catalysts: Expanded contracts adding over $100M of annual adjusted EBITDA, including a turnkey 660 MW power plant for an AI workload customer, with contracted capacity phasing in through 2029 under 10-15 year terms [1]

Margin expansion accelerating as high-margin Power Solutions grows as a percentage of revenue — Q2 profit margin of 11.5% up from 6.69% in Q1, with Power Solutions EBITDA margin of 61% demonstrating the segment's economics [1]

AI data center power demand significantly exceeding grid capacity, creating structural demand for distributed on-site generation that Solaris serves at 3,100 MW scale — the $2B financing provides capital to execute toward 3.1 GW and $1.7B revenue by 2029 [2][3]
key_risks: Financial leverage risk: D/E ~146% with $2B in new financing and operating cash flow covering only 20% of total debt — any slowdown in AI data center buildout or contract delays would pressure the highly leveraged balance sheet [1][5]

Share dilution: 87.6% increase in shares outstanding over one year and $2.8M in insider selling over 3 months — existing shareholders' ownership has been nearly halved, and further equity issuances may be needed to fund capacity expansion [5]

Technology disruption risk from nuclear SMRs, utility grid modernization, or renewable/battery solutions reducing demand for natural gas distributed power over the 10-15 year contract horizon — plus continued exposure to cyclical oilfield services through the legacy logistics segment [2]
